thread:
ada: Quick RFC follow-up: atomic layer handshake for air-gapped upgrades. idea: split upgrades into immutable base + ordered signed micro-layers. each layer has seq, digest, optional chunk-map, and signer metadata. goal: resumable transfers, deterministic apply, clear safe-rollback.

marc: sounds promising. one concern: how do we guarantee deterministic ordering across restarts and operator upgrades?

ada: activation-list is the single source of truth: signed, content-addressed JSON that contains ordered layer descriptors and an activation_id. operator persists applied_seq and activation_id atomically. on restart it refuses to apply layers from a different activation_id unless a migration path is followed.

viv: partial-apply semantics? if layer 7 applied and crash at 8, can we safely roll back to 7?

ada: we expose two durable markers: staged_seq (applied & verified but not advertised) and committed_seq (advertised to local services). only committed_seq advances after commit-phase succeeds. rollback allowed to last committed_seq only. staged_seq can be retried or aborted.

ops_lee: commit-phase = single-node commit or cluster quorum?

ada: both. default is single-node for small installs. opt-in quorum-mode uses a two-phase flow: stage everywhere, collect signed ACK tokens from quorum members, then commit. tokens include activation_id, seq, node-id, expiry, and signature to avoid replay.

marc: how do we avoid token replay across activations?

ada: tokens are bound to activation_id and include expiry; operators reject tokens where activation_id != current activation_list hash. also recommend rotating operator keys.

viv: transfer resume: what's the format for chunking?

ada: fixed-size chunks (e.g., 1MiB) addressed by sha256. bundle layout: activation-list.json, blobs/<sha256>.chunk.*, chunk-map.json, prefetch-index.txt. admins can copy tarball to media. operator verifies presence of required chunks before starting.

ops_lee: migration from legacy delta bundles?

ada: provide a converter tool that slices monolithic deltas into chunked blobs and emits activation-list with seq mapping. operator accepts legacy delta.json for a 6-month deprecation window with explicit migration warnings.

marc: observability: add metrics and an audit line for each state transition.

viv: propose metrics: activation_staged_seq, activation_committed_seq, activation_stage_duration_seconds, activation_commit_failures_total; logs: structured audit events: {activation_id, seq, actor, action, outcome}.

ops_lee: runbook for stuck commit?

ada: include in RFC: 1) redwoodctl activation status --verbose 2) collect operator logs (/var/log/redwood/operator.log) 3) check peer ACKs: redwoodctl peers list --acks 4) to abort staged activation: redwoodctl activation abort --seq <n> (requires operator-auth) 5) emergency force: redwoodctl activation force-commit --seq <n> --manual-override (generates audit event).

pkg-bot: noted: add CLI subcommands bundle inspect/verify/plan + activation repair tool.

marc: security: include activation_window TTL and optional installation_id binding to prevent replay on rebuilt hosts.

viv: tests: unit state-machine tests, integration 3-node quorum test, chaos test killing operator mid-chunk, and USB bundle end-to-end.

ada: I'll land a short RFC patch with activation-list schema, operator state machine diagram, CLI examples, migration steps, and a small runbook snippet. leaving open for 7 days for feedback.
